header_summary:
Recent discussions in the blockchain and cryptocurrency space have centered on several innovations and updates. A proposed mining strategy involving a tripwire proof aims to enhance security against 51% attacks by requiring adversaries to control a significantly larger portion of the hashrate. However, this strategy would necessitate a hard fork and poses risks of premature activation by dishonest parties, making consensus and careful planning essential for its successful implementation. For more information, visit [this link](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/UW5dOJNFjgt67sz-2sRUPeMJi0XL6_wSm7zKCmSoj_8IzkQavc-Vo9vwiR7Tbaz7bvP2YrH8b-1JGm-9jNQXQM8dqsw1f1Sl75SHIOt9cOc=@proton.me/T/#mb454f49ba0d6ff4b73f4bc28259cf2f9e1f96442).

In software development, Michael, known as fanquake, has released new Bitcoin test binaries that incorporate the latest glibc updates, enhancing compatibility and security across various architectures. This release underscores the importance of community feedback in refining Bitcoin software, as detailed on [GitHub](https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/releases/tag/static_bitcoind_db73d1623957).

Furthermore, an innovative open-source node editor has been developed to facilitate the building and testing of complex Bitcoin scripts, including vault mechanisms and delegation methods. This tool is particularly valuable for educational purposes, providing hands-on experience with script execution and cryptographic processes, directly in the user's browser. Examples and further details can be found [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/covenants-diy-a-node-editor-for-covenant-scripts/2826).

Lastly, advancements in cryptographic tools within the Rust programming environment include the development of `seedroller` and `keyderiver`, CLI tools designed for generating strong, random seeds and deriving keys. These tools exemplify the ongoing efforts to improve cryptographic security and are part of a broader initiative to minimize dependency on external libraries. Interested individuals can contribute to these projects by visiting [bitcoin-key-tools](https://github.com/bubb1es71/bitcoin-key-tools).

recent_posts.title: post-quantum: solution ideas to "tripwire"game-theory issues + a certificate-based rescue protocol
recent_posts.summary:
- A mining strategy with a tripwire proof increases attack difficulty for censors.
- Implementing this strategy requires a hard fork, posing risks of invalid block recognition.
- Alternative methods like UASF could mitigate miner collusion but complicate initial block downloads.

recent_posts.title: static-pie release binaries available for testing
recent_posts.summary: - Michael released new Bitcoin binaries with updated glibc on GitHub.  - Various formats and architectures are supported with security verification hashes.  - Community feedback is critical for the continued improvement of Bitcoin software.

recent_posts.title: Covenants.diy: a node editor for covenant scripts
recent_posts.summary:
- An open-source node editor has been developed for easy experimentation with covenant scripts.
- Each user-created graph receives a unique permalink, facilitating easy sharing and revisiting.
- The tool includes examples showcasing delay mechanisms, payout structures, and updated contractual states.

recent_posts.title: PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format
recent_posts.summary: - The paper backup system now has improved data integrity and security features.  - A two-byte CRC16 checksum has been added for enhanced reliability before KDF processes.  - The backup structure includes versioning, salt, initialization vector, and ciphertext components.

recent_posts.title: Seedroller and keyderiver: cli tools to generate BIP39 seed words and derive BIP380 keys
recent_posts.summary: - `Seedroller` generates BIP39 seeds using dice and system entropy in Rust.  - `Keyderiver` converts those seeds into BIP380 keys, also minimizing external dependencies.  - Both tools are open for enhancement by community feedback on GitHub.

active_posts.title: Giving teeth to expected EC disabling: P2XX(-T)(-ML)
active_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin developers propose P2TRv2 enhancement methods due to quantum computing threats.
- Two proposals, Tripwire and Miner Lockdown, aim for timely disabling of EC opcodes.
- Integration into consensus rules ensures reliable activation without additional forks.

active_posts.title: DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
active_posts.summary:
- DropKick aids Bitcoin users by implementing a commit/reveal protocol on the blockchain.
- The protocol uses a trustless timestamping feature to protect against quantum threats.
- DropKick's implementation consumes minimal blockchain space and utilizes third-party aggregators.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Anti-Fee-Sniping with LockTime
active_posts.summary: - The nLockTime and nSequence features in Bitcoin are formalized in BIP326.  - Stability and integrity in transactions are enhanced by specific non-reset conditions.  - The BIP aims to improve privacy and efficiency in Bitcoin with technical adjustments.

active_posts.title: Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data?
active_posts.summary: - Enhancing blockchain for post-quantum cryptography introduces new system elements and blocks.  - Implementing these changes requires significant updates to mining and network protocols.  - Alternative solutions could streamline integration while increasing storage needs.

active_posts.title: PQC output type discussion
active_posts.summary:
- The email proposes a P2TRv2 output type for quick, emergency PQC adoption in Bitcoin.
- A dual strategy is discussed, planning for long-term migration via a P2MR-based output type.
- The debate highlights varying opinions on the timing of disabling ECC due to quantum threats.

active_posts.title: Running Core's real consensus code inside a zkVM
active_posts.summary:
- Hazync preserves Bitcoin Core logic using `riscv32im` in a RISC0 zkVM for consensus proofs.
- It reduces computational demand by verifying block proofs against validated prior proofs.
- Community can participate in proof generation and verify independently via a browser tool.

today_in_history_posts.title: Capital Efficient Honeypots w/ "Scorched Earth" Doublespending Protection
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Bitcoin-based honeypots use rewards to expose server intrusions through public blockchain data.
- Implementing such honeypots with 2-of-2 multisig and SIGHASH_SINGLE aligns with current Bitcoin protocols.
- The "scorched earth" method increases honeypot reward credibility at a cost to the owner.

today_in_history_posts.title: Testing a Flare-like routing implementation on 2500 AWS nodes
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Flare is a Lightning Network routing protocol utilizing local and remote path mappings.
- Implementation tests showed high routing success, except one case with only 20% success.
- The protocol assumes an undirected network, but actual channel directions affect routing.

today_in_history_posts.title: Non interactive anti-exfil (airgap compatible)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The new anti-exfiltration protocol enhances security for air-gapped PSBT devices.  - It integrates cryptographic operations and nonces to safely sign Bitcoin transactions.  - Verification ensures the integrity of signatures with rigorous recalculations and checks.
